key_big: To evaluate, put the value in brackets in place of the variable, then follow the order of operations.

body_html:
Write expressions from words

An expression uses numbers, variables and operations, like 3x + 5. A number next to a variable means multiply: 3x = 3 × x.

WordsExpression
the sum of n and 7n + 7
8 less than mm − 8
the product of 4 and y4y
the quotient of n and 5n5
7 times the sum of x and 27(x + 2)

“Less than” and “subtracted from” switch the order: “8 less than m” is m − 8, not 8 − m.

Evaluate by substitution

To evaluate an expression, replace each variable with its value in brackets. Then follow the order of operations: brackets, exponents, × and ÷, then + and −.

Example 1

Evaluate 2a + 3b when a = 5 and b = 4.

2 × 5 = 10 and 3 × 4 = 12. Then 10 + 12 = 22.

Answer: 22

Example 2

Evaluate 5 − 2y when y = −3.

2 × (−3) = −6. Then 5 − (−6) = 5 + 6 = 11.

Answer: 11

Example 3

Evaluate 2y − 13 when y = 56.

2 × 56 = 106 = 53. Then 53 − 13 = 43.

Answer: 1 13

Cost formulas

Many prices have a start fee plus a price for each hour or item. The price per hour is the coefficient, and the start fee is the constant.

Example 4

Use C = 12h + 15 to find the cost of a 3-hour kayak rental.

12 × 3 = 36. Then 36 + 15 = 51.

Answer: $51.00

MistakeWhat to do instead

“8 less than m” = 8 − mStart with m and take 8 away: m − 8
4 × (−5) = 20Positive × negative is negative: −20
(−3)2 = −9(−3) × (−3) = 9
6 − (−2) = 4Subtracting a negative is adding: 6 + 2 = 8
20 − 3y = 17yMultiply before you subtract: 20 − 3 × 4 = 8

faq.q: What does substitution mean in Grade 8 math?
faq.a: Substitution means replacing a variable with a number and then working out the value. For 3x + 5 when x = 4, write 3 × (4) + 5 = 17.
No. A number next to a variable means multiply, so 3x = 3 × x. When x = 5, 3x is 15, not 8 and not 35.

faq.q: How do you evaluate an expression with a negative number?
faq.a: Put the negative number in brackets and use the integer sign rules. For 5 − 2y when y = −3: 2 × (−3) = −6, and 5 − (−6) = 11.

faq.q: Are expressions and substitution in the BC Grade 8 math curriculum?
faq.a: Yes. The BC Grade 8 Patterning standards include writing expressions and evaluating them using substitution, with whole numbers, integers, fractions and decimals.

items.e: A number written next to a variable means multiply: 3x = 3 × x. It is not 3 + x, and when x = 5 it is 15, not 35.

items.q: Which expression means “the sum of a number n and 7”?
items.e: “Sum” means add: n + 7. (7n is a product, not a sum.)

items.q: Which expression means “6 more than a number x”?
items.e: “6 more than x” means add 6 to x: x + 6. (6x means 6 × x.)

items.q: Which expression means “the product of 4 and a number y”?
items.e: “Product” means multiply: 4 × y = 4y. (4 + y is a sum.)

items.q: Which expression means “8 less than a number m”?
items.e: Start with m and take 8 away: m − 8. The order matters: 8 − m means “m less than 8”.

items.q: Chloe earns $15 an hour babysitting. Which expression gives what she earns in h hours?
items.e: Each hour adds $15, so h hours give 15 × h = 15h. (15 + h adds only one $15.)

items.q: Which expression means “a number x decreased by 3”?
items.e: “Decreased by 3” means subtract 3 from x: x − 3. (3 − x subtracts in the wrong order.)
“Twice” means 2 times: 2k. (k2 means k × k, not 2 × k.)

items.q: Which expression means “the quotient of a number n and 5”?
items.e: “Quotient” means divide, in the order given: n ÷ 5 = n5. (5n divides in the wrong order.)

items.q: Which expression means “10 subtracted from a number x”?
items.e: Start with x and subtract 10: x − 10. (10 − x puts the numbers in the order they are read, which is wrong here.)

items.q: Which expression means “a number n multiplied by −2”?
items.e: Multiply n by −2: −2n. (n − 2 subtracts 2 instead of multiplying.)

items.q: The temperature on Grouse Mountain is t °C. Overnight it drops 6 °C. Which expression gives the new temperature?
items.e: A drop of 6 °C means subtract 6: t − 6. (−6t multiplies instead of subtracting.)

items.q: Which expression means “5 more than 3 times a number x”?
items.e: 3 times x is 3x, then add 5: 3x + 5. (3 + x + 5 reads 3x as 3 + x. 3(x + 5) multiplies the 5 too.)

items.q: Which expression means “5 less than 3 times a number p”?
items.e: 3 times p is 3p; 5 less than that is 3p − 5. (5 − 3p subtracts in the wrong order.)

items.q: Which expression means “half of a number w, minus 4”?
items.e: Half of w is w2; then subtract 4: w2 − 4. (2w is double, not half.)

items.q: Which expression means “7 times the sum of a number x and 2”?
items.e: Find the sum first, so it goes in brackets: 7(x + 2). (7x + 2 multiplies only x by 7.)

items.q: Ava has x stickers. Mateo has 4 fewer than 3 times as many stickers as Ava. Which expression gives the number of stickers Mateo has?
items.e: 3 times as many as Ava is 3x; 4 fewer is 3x − 4. (3x + 4 means 4 more, not 4 fewer.)

items.q: Which expression means “the difference of a number y and 9, divided by 4”?
items.e: The difference y − 9 is found first, then divided by 4: y − 94. (y4 − 9 divides only y.)

items.q: The perimeter of a rectangle is P = 2l + 2w. What is P for this rectangle?
items.e: 2 × 9 + 2 × 4 = 18 + 8 = 26, so 26 cm. (13 cm adds only two sides. 36 is 9 × 4, the area. 22 doubles only the length.)

items.q: The area of a triangle is A = bh2. What is A for this triangle?
items.e: 10 × 7 = 70, then 70 ÷ 2 = 35, so 35 cm<sup>2</sup>. (70 forgets to divide by 2. 17 adds 10 + 7 instead of multiplying. 34 doubles 10 + 7.)

items.q: Evaluate a − b2 when a = −3 and b = 7.
items.e: Top first: −3 − 7 = −10. Then −10 ÷ 2 = −5. (2 works out −3 + 7. 5 is a sign error.)
(−4)2 = 16. Then 10 − 16 = −6. (26 uses −16 for the square. 18 reads x2 as 2x.)

2.5 × 4 = 10. (6.5 adds. 8.5 multiplies only the 2 by 4. 100 forgets the decimal point: 25 × 4.)
Line up the decimal points: 2.7 + 1.4 = 4.1. (3.11 adds the tenths as 7 + 4 = 11 without carrying.)

items.q: Evaluate x + 34 when x = 12.
items.e: Use a common denominator: 24 + 34 = 54 = 1 14. (46 adds the tops and the bottoms. 38 multiplies.)
0.3 × 0.3 = 0.09: 3 × 3 = 9, with 2 decimal places. (0.9 has too few decimal places. 0.6 doubles instead of squaring.)
Brackets first: 6 − 2 = 4. Then 1.5 × 4 = 6. (7 multiplies only x: 9 − 2. 4 forgets the 1.5. −6 subtracts in the wrong order: 1.5 × (2 − 6).)

items.q: Evaluate 2y − 13 when y = 56.
items.e: 2 × 56 = 106 = 53. Then 53 − 13 = 43 = 1 13. (12 forgets the 2. 2 adds the 13.)
3 = 2 55, so 2 55 − 25 = 2 35. (15 subtracts only the tops. 3 25 adds.)
8 ÷ 4 = 2, then 2 × 3 = 6. Negative × negative is positive, so the answer is 6. (−6 is a sign error. 10 23 multiplies by 43.)

items.q: Evaluate xy when x = −9 and y = 6.
items.e: −9 ÷ 6 = −96 = −1 12. (1 12 is a sign error. −23 divides in the wrong order. −54 multiplies.)
23 × 23 = 49: square the top and the bottom. (43 squares only the top. 29 squares only the bottom.)

items.q: Evaluate x2 + x3 when x = 12.
items.e: 12 ÷ 2 = 6 and 12 ÷ 3 = 4. Then 6 + 4 = 10. (125 adds the denominators. 24 multiplies 6 × 4.)

items.q: Evaluate ab when a = 34 and b = −29.
items.e: 34 × (−29) = −636 = −16. Positive × negative is negative. (16 is a sign error. −513 adds the tops and the bottoms. −278 divides.)
6 × 34 = 184 = 4.5. Then 4.5 − 2.5 = 2. (7 adds the 2.5. −1.75 multiplies the top and the bottom by 6: 1824 = 0.75. 3.5 forgets x: 6 − 2.5.)

items.q: The cost in dollars to rent a kayak in Deep Cove for h hours is C = 12h + 15. What does a 3-hour rental cost?
items.e: 12 × 3 = 36, then 36 + 15 = 51, so $51.00. ($81.00 multiplies 27 × 3. $30.00 reads 12h as 12 + 3. $57.00 multiplies the $15 by 3 instead.)

items.q: Bike rental at Stanley Park costs $8 to start plus $6 for each hour. Which expression gives the cost in dollars for h hours?
items.e: $6 for each hour is 6h; add the $8 start fee once: 6h + 8. (8h + 6 mixes up the two prices. h + 14 reads 6h as 6 + h.)

items.q: The bike rental costs 6h + 8 dollars for h hours. What does a 4-hour rental cost?
A pizza costs $14, and delivery is $5 for the whole order. Which expression gives the cost in dollars of p pizzas with delivery?
items.e: p pizzas cost 14p; delivery is added once: 14p + 5. (19p charges delivery for every pizza.)

items.q: A taxi in Victoria charges $3.50 to start plus $2.00 for each kilometre. The cost in dollars is C = 3.5 + 2k for k kilometres. What does an 8 km ride cost?
Ski rental in Whistler costs $45 a day plus a $10 helmet fee for the whole rental: C = 45d + 10. What do 3 days cost?
items.e: 45 × 3 = 135, then 135 + 10 = 145, so $145.00. ($165.00 charges the helmet fee every day. $135.00 forgets the helmet fee.)

items.q: A family drives onto a ferry to Vancouver Island. The cost in dollars is C = 19p + 65 for p people. What does the trip cost for 4 people?
items.e: 19 × 4 = 76, then 76 + 65 = 141, so $141.00. ($336.00 works out 84 × 4. $88.00 reads 19p as 19 + 4. $279.00 multiplies the car fare by 4 instead.)

items.q: A pool pass costs $40, and then each visit costs $2.50. Which expression gives the cost in dollars for v visits?
items.e: Each visit is $2.50, so v visits cost 2.5v; the pass is added once: 2.5v + 40.

items.q: The pool costs 2.5v + 40 dollars for v visits. What do 12 visits cost?
Concert tickets cost $28 each plus a $6 fee for the order: C = 28t + 6. What do 5 tickets cost?
items.e: 28 × 5 = 140, then 140 + 6 = 146, so $146.00. ($170.00 charges the fee on every ticket. $140.00 forgets the fee.)

items.q: For the Terry Fox Run, the Grade 8 class spends $30 on supplies and sells cookies for $2 each. Which expression gives their profit in dollars for c cookies?
items.e: Money in: 2c. Money out: 30. Profit = 2c − 30. (30 − 2c subtracts in the wrong order. 2c + 30 adds the cost instead of subtracting it.)

items.q: The class’s profit is 2c − 30 dollars for c cookies. What is the profit if they sell only 12 cookies?
items.e: 2 × 12 = 24, then 24 − 30 = −6. A profit of −$6.00 means they lost $6.00. ($54.00 adds the 30. $6.00 drops the minus sign.)

items.q: Owen has a $50 gift card for a smoothie shop. Each smoothie costs $6.50, so the amount left is B = 50 − 6.5s after s smoothies. How much is left after 4 smoothies?
Apples cost $0.75 each at a Kelowna fruit stand. The cost in dollars is 0.75a for a apples. What do 8 apples cost?
items.e: 0.75 × 8 = 6, so $6.00. ($8.75 adds 0.75 + 8. $60.00 and $0.60 put the decimal point in the wrong place.)

items.q: A phone plan costs $35 a month plus $0.20 for each megabyte of data over the limit: C = 35 + 0.2d. What is the bill when d = 45?
At a hockey game, an adult ticket costs x dollars and a student ticket costs $4 less. Which expression gives the cost of 3 adult tickets and 2 student tickets?
items.e: Adults: 3x. Students: 2(x − 4) = 2x − 8. Total: 5x − 8. (5x − 4 takes $4 off only once. 5x − 12 takes $4 off the 3 adult tickets instead.)

items.q: The hockey tickets cost 5x − 8 dollars. What is the total when an adult ticket costs $18?
A canoe rental on the Fraser River costs $20 for 1 hour, $26 for 2 hours and $32 for 3 hours. Which expression gives the cost in dollars for h hours?
items.e: Each extra hour adds $6, so the expression has 6h. For 1 hour: 6 + ? = 20, so the start fee is $14: 6h + 14. Check: 6 × 3 + 14 = 32. (6h + 20 gives $26 for 1 hour.)

items.q: Plan A for a paddleboard costs 8h + 10 dollars and Plan B costs 10h dollars for h hours. Which plan is cheaper for 4 hours, and by how much?
Team T-shirts cost $12 each and hoodies cost $18 each, so an order costs 12s + 18h dollars. What does an order of 10 T-shirts and 5 hoodies cost?
